scenes.visual: marble beakers: same red marbles, smaller pile, specific activity up; three numbers
scenes.narration: Three numbers run every purification. Specific activity is enzyme units divided by total protein — the fraction of your sample that is the target, and it must rise at every good step. Fold-purification is the final specific activity divided by the starting one. Percent yield is how much of your original activity you kept. Picture a beaker of mixed marbles: the same number of red marbles in a smaller pile is a higher specific activity.

scenes.visual: four panels: salting out curve, gel filtration, ion exchange, affinity
scenes.narration: Four physical properties, four columns. Solubility: salting out with ammonium sulfate drops proteins out of solution at different salt concentrations. Size: gel filtration, where — counterintuitively — the large proteins exit first. Charge: ion exchange, where opposite charges stick to the beads. Binding affinity: a bead decorated with something only your protein recognizes. Match the method to whatever you already know about your target.

scenes.visual: charged beads capture proteins; pH vs pI; salt gradient elutes
scenes.narration: Ion exchange separates by charge, and the rule is just opposites attract. A cation exchanger carries negative beads and binds positive proteins — use it when the buffer pH is below your protein's pI. An anion exchanger carries positive beads and binds negative proteins — use it when pH is above the pI. Once bound, raise the salt or shift the pH and your protein lets go.

scenes.visual: gel lanes; bands migrate by size; purification lanes collapse to one band
scenes.narration: SDS coats every protein with uniform negative charge, so the gel sorts by size alone — small proteins migrate faster, toward the bottom. Reading it: fewer bands means a purer sample; a band's position gives molecular weight, compared to the ladder; band intensity reflects how much protein is there. The goal of a purification is a single band — one protein, finally alone.
scenes.slideTitle: How to read an SDS-PAGE gel

scenes.visual: laser, flight tube, spectrum of peaks; time of flight vs mass
scenes.narration: Mass spectrometry weighs molecules to identify them. In MALDI-TOF, a laser blasts your protein off a matrix-coated plate and ionizes it; the ions fly down an evacuated tube, and the time of flight tells you the mass — heavier ions arrive later. It needs only picomoles of sample and can resolve proteins above ten kilodaltons. Weigh a protein's tryptic peptides and you can identify it from a database.
